from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

sections.title: Introduction: The Privacy Paradox
sections.content: Define the challenge of contact tracing: identifying exposure to an infected person without revealing individual identities or locations. Introduce the core trade-off: public health safety vs. user anonymity.
sections.example: Imagine Alice and Bob. Alice is infected. How does Bob know he was near Alice without a central server knowing Alice's name or where they met?

sections.title: Prerequisite: Cryptographic Hashing
sections.content: Explain one-way functions (hashing). A hash turns data into a fixed-length string that cannot be reversed. This ensures we identify a device without knowing who owns it.
sections.example: Visual: Input 'Alice' -> [Hash Function] -> 'a7f3...'. If you see 'a7f3...', you cannot figure out it was 'Alice', but you can verify it's the same person if the input remains consistent.

sections.title: Step 1: Ephemeral Identifier Generation
sections.content: Explain how devices generate a Daily Tracing Key (DTK) and derive ephemeral IDs (EphIDs) from it. These IDs rotate every 15-20 minutes to prevent tracking.
sections.example: Visual: A timeline showing Device A generating ID_1 at 10:00, ID_2 at 10:15, and ID_3 at 10:30. These IDs look random and disconnected to any observer.

sections.title: Step 2: Proximity Exchange & Storage
sections.content: Devices broadcast their current EphID via Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). Nearby devices 'hear' these IDs and store them locally in a secure log on their own phones.
sections.example: Visual: Alice and Bob stand close. Alice's phone sends 'EphID_A'. Bob's phone records 'EphID_A' in his local 'History Log' folder, hidden from the cloud.

sections.title: Step 3: The Match Process
sections.content: If Alice tests positive, she uploads her secret DTKs to a public server. Bob’s phone downloads these DTKs, regenerates Alice's past EphIDs locally, and checks if any match the logs in his phone.
sections.example: Visual: A 'Match Found' animation. Bob's phone runs a local check: [My Log] vs [Alice's Regenerated IDs]. If a match exists, a notification pops up: 'You have been in contact with an infected person'.

storyboard.title: Step 1: Ephemeral Identifier Generation
lecture_lines: Observed IDs appear random and disconnected.
animations: Display 'Daily Tracing Key' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/key.svg] rotating into an 'Ephemeral ID Generator' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/generator.svg]. Color DTK #EFC050, Generator #6B5B95.
Animate a timeline [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/timeline.svg] with timestamps appearing and distinct IDs generated. Color ID_1 #FF6F61, ID_2 #88B04B, ID_3 #D64161.

storyboard.title: Step 2: Proximity Exchange & Storage
lecture_lines: Phones broadcast ephemeral identifiers via Bluetooth.
Nearby phones record these identifiers locally.
History logs remain secure on devices.
animations: Represent [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/alice.svg] Alice and [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bob.svg] Bob as dots with BLE signals broadcasting. Color AliceSignal #FF6F61, BobSignal #6B5B95.
Animate the EphID traveling from [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] Alice's phone to Bob's phone. Color EphID #88B04B.
Display 'History Log' appearing on [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] Bob's phone, storing the ID. Color Log #EFC050.

storyboard.title: Step 3: The Match Process
lecture_lines: Positive users upload keys to servers.
Phones download keys to check matches.
Local matching alerts users of exposure.
animations: Show Alice uploading DTK to a public 'Match Server' [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/server.svg]. Color Server #88B04B, DTK #EFC050.
Animate Bob's phone [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] downloading the DTK and regenerating IDs locally. Color RegeneratedIDs #6B5B95.
Display 'Match Found' pop-up on Bob's phone [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] screen as the logs cross-reference. Color Match #D64161.
